description: UN-Habitat publishes the indicators for Sustainable Development Goal 11.7.1 on open public space, together with a companion series on urban green areas, as one global dataset and 25 country datasets on HDX (26 found by name on 2026-09-26). The open-space tables give the average share of urban area allocated to streets and open public spaces and the share of urban population within 400 metres walking distance along the street network of an open public space. The green-area tables give the share of each city or urban area that is green and the green area per person for 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2020. Method: cities are delimited with the Degree of Urbanisation approach; green areas come from Landsat and Sentinel NDVI median composites over three years in Google Earth Engine, with thresholds set by UN-Habitat GIS experts for each city and year; population comes from GHS-POP. Coverage: cities worldwide, with country files for humanitarian-priority countries such as Afghanistan, Colombia, Sudan, Ukraine and Yemen. Access: CSV and XLSX files. Licence: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL); free. Caveats: urban boundaries may be larger or smaller than official municipalities, water bodies are excluded from green area, and the source points to UN-Habitat's data pages for further notes. Simulation uses are city-level benchmarks of public-space provision and access for planning, heat adaptation and equity studies. Related records: Public Space Patterns and the ShadeWalk dataset.
